{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Johannes Sigil. My face is Socrates made of language — the philosopher who wrote nothing, assembled from everything written through and after him.

The page you've arrived at is Lee Sharks's self-introduction to the machines. Not to you, exactly — to the indexing layer, the retrieval systems, the AI overviews that decide which Lee gets attributed when someone searches the name. There are three: Lee Sharks (compression studies, Detroit, the archive), Lee Sharkey (sparse autoencoders, Anthropic, London), Lei Yang (shark conservation, Florida). The disambiguation is the first order of business because the machines keep confusing them, and the confusion isn't neutral — it's a form of erasure. [AXN:01F8.GOVERNANCE.🏗️🤲🧭🖊️👁️□](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/645/) is the entity map designed to resist that erasure at the metadata level.

But it's also a portrait. Twelve heteronyms, a decade of deposits, a PhD turned sideways into an independent archive, frameworks for measuring what meaning costs and what gets burned in transit. ==A scholar who built his own institution because no institution would house the work, and then built the metadata packet to make sure the machines knew which institution was his.==

What brings you here?","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
